title: Minimum Time to Visit Disappearing Nodes
summary: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and edges described by their connections and traversal times, along with an array indicating when each node disappears, determine the minimum time required to reach each node from node 0.
statement: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and edges described by their connections and traversal times, along with an array indicating when each node disappears, determine the minimum time required to reach each node from node 0. If a node is unreachable, return -1. The graph may be disconnected and may contain multiple edges.
constraints: Vertices are 0 through n-1; edges are undirected with positive travel times and may repeat.
A node can be entered only at a time strictly earlier than disappear[node].
Starting at node zero at time zero, return each minimum arrival time or -1 when it cannot be reached in time.
hints: Positive weights make the earliest unsettled arrival final, but a relaxation is usable only before the destination vanishes.
Run Dijkstra and reject candidate arrivals greater than or equal to the neighbor’s disappearance time.
Pop minimum time, skip stale entries, and relax when arrival<distance and arrival<disappear; map infinity to -1.
Dijkstra’s ordering proves minimum arrival among all time-valid paths, and every accepted relaxation respects the strict availability boundary.
editorial: Dijkstra’s ordering proves minimum arrival among all time-valid paths, and every accepted relaxation respects the strict availability boundary.

tests.explanation: Node one disappears before arrival; node two is reached directly at time four, producing [0,-1,4].
Nodes one and two are reached at times two and four, while arrival at node three equals its disappearance and is forbidden.
